A.explanation: Up at P and down at Q would imply the beam is in tension, but the weight of the unit above pushes the strut into compression.

B.explanation: Down-right at P and up-left at Q are both directed along the beam toward its centre, showing compression of the strut with balanced horizontal and vertical components.

C.explanation: Left at P and right at Q give a resultant that is not along the beam and cannot balance moments about Q for this strut.

D.explanation: Up at P is wrong because the air-conditioning unit loads the top pin P downward onto the beam.

hints: Notice the beam PQ is a diagonal strut with P under the heavy unit and Q pinned to the wall - decide if the unit squeezes or stretches the beam.
For a light strut in equilibrium with only end forces, the resultant at each end must act along the line PQ to give zero moment, so resolve that direction into horizontal and vertical components.
At P the along-beam direction is down and to the right toward Q, so check which diagram pairs this with the opposite up-left direction at Q.
walkthrough: Identify the system as the light rigid beam PQ. Pin P carries the weight of the air-conditioning unit above, so the contact force on the beam at P has a downward vertical component.
The beam is a two-force strut between pins P and Q. For zero resultant force and zero resultant moment, the two resultants must be equal, opposite and collinear with the line joining P to Q.
The unit pushes down on P, so the beam is squeezed between P and Q. It is in compression, not tension.
In compression each end is pushed toward the centre of the beam. At the top end P the centre direction is down and to the right, so $F_{Px}$ is to the right and $F_{Py}$ is down.
At the bottom end Q the centre direction is up and to the left, so $F_{Qx}$ is to the left and $F_{Qy}$ is up. Then $\sum F_x = 0$ and $\sum F_y = 0$.
Moments also balance because both resultants act along PQ, so their perpendicular distance from the line of action is zero and net moment about either end is zero.
Only diagram B shows right plus down at the top and left plus up at the bottom, both along the beam. This is option B.
